---- MODULE W4Od9m4p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Reqs == {1, 2, 3}
Cap  == 2
Load == [r \in Reqs |-> IF r = 3 THEN 2 ELSE 1]
QueueMax == 2

Sum(S) == LET f[T \in SUBSET Reqs] ==
              IF T = {} THEN 0
              ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in T : TRUE
                   IN Load[x] + f[T \ {x}]
          IN f[S]

VARIABLES waiting, drawing, done, shed
vars == <<waiting, drawing, done, shed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ waiting \subseteq Reqs
    /\ drawing \subseteq Reqs
    /\ done    \subseteq Reqs
    /\ shed    \subseteq Reqs

Unqueued == Reqs \ (waiting \cup drawing \cup done \cup shed)

Init ==
    /\ waiting = {}
    /\ drawing = {}
    /\ done    = {}
    /\ shed    = {}

Admit(r) ==
    /\ r \in Unqueued
    /\ Cardinality(waiting) < QueueMax
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<drawing, done, shed>>

ShedReq(r) ==
    /\ r \in Unqueued
    /\ Cardinality(waiting) >= QueueMax
    /\ shed' = shed \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, drawing, done>>

Start(r) ==
    /\ r \in waiting
    /\ Sum(drawing) + Load[r] <= Cap
    /\ drawing' = drawing \cup {r}
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<done, shed>>

Finish(r) ==
    /\ r \in drawing
    /\ drawing' = drawing \ {r}
    /\ done'    = done \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, shed>>

Resolved == Reqs = (done \cup shed)

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Admit(r)
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : ShedReq(r)
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Start(r)
    \/ \E r \in Reqs : Finish(r)
    \/ (Resolved /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityRespected == Sum(drawing) <= Cap
====
nl: A power-grid load shedder manages incoming load requests against a bounded grid capacity. Each request draws a fixed amount of power. The system holds a small bounded admission queue with backpressure: when the queue is full, further requests are shed rather than queued. Requests may be admitted, shed, started, or finished in any order (messages can be reordered, so there is no FIFO guarantee). A request may be admitted to the queue only if the queue has room; if the queue is full an unqueued request is shed instead. A queued request may be started (begin drawing power) only if the total power drawn by all currently drawing requests plus this request's load stays within grid capacity. A drawing request may finish, freeing its capacity. SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state the total power drawn by all currently drawing requests never exceeds the grid capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od17m2p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Bags == {1, 2, 3}
Part == {1, 2, 3}
None == 0

VARIABLES atSrc, inflight, delivered, target, crashed
vars == <<atSrc, inflight, delivered, target, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ atSrc \subseteq Bags
    /\ inflight \subseteq Bags
    /\ delivered \subseteq Bags
    /\ target \in [Bags -> Part \cup {None}]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Part

Init ==
    /\ atSrc = Bags
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ delivered = {}
    /\ target = [b \in Bags |-> None]
    /\ crashed = {}

\* Phase 1: reserve a bag at the source and route it toward a participant.
Prepare(b, p) ==
    /\ b \in atSrc
    /\ atSrc' = atSrc \ {b}
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {b}
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![b] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<delivered, crashed>>

\* Phase 2 commit: the routed participant is alive, so hand the bag over.
Commit(b) ==
    /\ b \in inflight
    /\ target[b] \notin crashed
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {b}
    /\ delivered' = delivered \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<atSrc, target, crashed>>

\* Phase 2 abort: the routed participant crashed silently; return the bag.
Abort(b) ==
    /\ b \in inflight
    /\ target[b] \in crashed
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {b}
    /\ atSrc' = atSrc \cup {b}
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![b] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<delivered, crashed>>

\* A participant crashes silently.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<atSrc, inflight, delivered, target>>

Done == (delivered = Bags) /\ (crashed = Part)

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bags, p \in Part : Prepare(b, p)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Commit(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Abort(b)
    \/ \E p \in Part : Crash(p)
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every bag sits in exactly one location: no bag is created or destroyed.
Conservation ==
    /\ (atSrc \cup inflight \cup delivered) = Bags
    /\ atSrc \cap inflight = {}
    /\ atSrc \cap delivered = {}
    /\ inflight \cap delivered = {}
====
nl: An airport baggage router moves a fixed set of bags from a source belt to a set of downstream participant sorters using a two-phase commit protocol. Each bag starts at the source. In the Prepare action a bag is reserved at the source and routed toward a chosen participant, moving it into an in-flight state. In the Commit action an in-flight bag whose routed participant is still alive is handed over and marked delivered. In the Abort action an in-flight bag whose routed participant has crashed silently is returned to the source so it can be re-routed later. In the Crash action a participant fails silently, after which any bag routed to it must be aborted rather than committed. Because one participant can crash silently at any time, a bag may cycle between the source and the in-flight state before finally being delivered to a live participant. SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state each bag resides in exactly one of the source, in-flight, or delivered locations, so the total collection of bags is neither created nor destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od12m9p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Slots == {1, 2, 3}
Reqs == {1, 2}
MaxEpoch == 2
Free == 0

Msgs == Reqs \X Slots \X (0 .. MaxEpoch)

VARIABLES epoch, owner, inbox, log, sent
vars == <<epoch, owner, inbox, log, sent>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Reqs \cup {Free}]
    /\ inbox \subseteq Msgs
    /\ log \subseteq (Slots \X Reqs)
    /\ sent \subseteq (Reqs \X Slots)

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ log = {}
    /\ sent = {}

\* A request for a storage slot is emitted, tagged with the current epoch.
Emit(r, s) ==
    /\ <<r, s>> \notin sent
    /\ sent' = sent \cup {<<r, s>>}
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {<<r, s, epoch>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, log>>

\* A fresh request for a free slot is granted and recorded in the log.
Grant(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m[3] = epoch
    /\ owner[m[2]] = Free
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![m[2]] = m[1]]
    /\ log' = log \cup {<<m[2], m[1]>>}
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, sent>>

\* A stale (wrong-epoch) or already-taken request is dropped.
Reject(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ (m[3] # epoch \/ owner[m[2]] # Free)
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, log, sent>>

\* Reconfiguration bumps the epoch, invalidating in-flight stale requests.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inbox, log, sent>>

Done == (inbox = {}) /\ (epoch = MaxEpoch) /\ (sent = Reqs \X Slots)

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Reqs, s \in Slots : Emit(r, s)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Grant(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Reject(m)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No slot is ever double-allocated: any request the log records for a slot
\* is that slot's one current owner.
NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A s \in Slots : \A r \in Reqs :
        (<<s, r>> \in log) => (owner[s] = r)
====
nl: A blood-bank inventory tracker allocates storage slots to incoming requisition requests under epoch-numbered reconfiguration. Because messages can be reordered, requests sit in an unordered inbox and are processed in any order. In the Emit action a request for a specific slot is created and stamped with the epoch current at emission time, and each request-slot pair is emitted at most once. In the Grant action a request whose stamped epoch still matches the current epoch and whose target slot is free is granted: the slot's owner is set and the allocation is appended to a permanent log. In the Reject action a request that is stale (its stamped epoch no longer matches) or whose slot is already taken is silently dropped from the inbox. In the Reconfigure action the tracker advances to a new epoch, which invalidates any still-pending stale requests. SAFETY PROPERTY: for every slot, any request ever recorded in the allocation log as holding that slot is exactly the slot's current owner, so no slot is double-allocated to two different requests.

---- MODULE W4Od5m0p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Inst == {1, 2}
Slots == {1, 2}
Players == {1, 2}
MaxVer == 2
Empty == 0

VARIABLES version, board, cache, history, admitted
vars == <<version, board, cache, history, admitted>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0 .. MaxVer
    /\ board \in [Slots -> Players \cup {Empty}]
    /\ cache \in [Inst -> 0 .. MaxVer]
    /\ history \in Seq(0 .. MaxVer)
    /\ admitted \subseteq Players

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ board = [s \in Slots |-> Empty]
    /\ cache = [i \in Inst |-> 0]
    /\ history = << >>
    /\ admitted = {}

\* An instance refreshes its optimistic snapshot of the shared pool version.
Sync(i) ==
    /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![i] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, board, history, admitted>>

\* A player is authorized (admitted) into the shared matchmaking pool.
Admit(p) ==
    /\ p \notin admitted
    /\ admitted' = admitted \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, board, cache, history>>

\* Compare-and-swap seat placement: only a non-stale instance whose cached
\* version equals the live version may commit, and only for an admitted player.
Place(i, s, p) ==
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ cache[i] = version
    /\ p \in admitted
    /\ board[s] = Empty
    /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![s] = p]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![i] = version + 1]
    /\ history' = Append(history, cache[i])
    /\ UNCHANGED admitted

\* Compare-and-swap seat removal by a non-stale instance.
Vacate(i, s) ==
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ cache[i] = version
    /\ board[s] # Empty
    /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![s] = Empty]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![i] = version + 1]
    /\ history' = Append(history, cache[i])
    /\ UNCHANGED admitted

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Sync(i)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Admit(p)
    \/ \E i \in Inst, s \in Slots, p \in Players : Place(i, s, p)
    \/ \E i \in Inst, s \in Slots : Vacate(i, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No stale participant's write ever takes effect: the version basis recorded
\* by each committed write forms the contiguous sequence 0, 1, 2, ...
LogContiguous == \A k \in 1 .. Len(history) : history[k] = k - 1
====
nl: A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats admitted players onto a shared board of lobby slots. Two independent matchmaker instances share the one pool and coordinate through optimistic locking with retry: a shared version counter guards every write. In the Sync action an instance refreshes its cached snapshot of the current pool version. In the Admit action a player is authorized into the shared pool. In the Place action an instance seats an admitted player into an empty slot, but only as a compare-and-swap: the instance may commit only if its cached version still equals the live version, after which the version is bumped and the basis version it used is appended to a history log; a stale instance whose cached version lags must Sync and retry instead. In the Vacate action a non-stale instance likewise compare-and-swaps a seated player out of a slot, bumping the version and logging its basis. Because the two instances share one pool, a write by a stale instance would clobber the other's update, so such writes are rejected. SAFETY PROPERTY: the basis versions recorded by the committed writes form the contiguous sequence 0, 1, 2, ..., so no stale or unauthorized instance's write ever takes effect.

---- MODULE W4Od15m9p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Orders == {1, 2, 3}
Slots == {1, 2}
MaxEpoch == 2
NoSlot == 0

VARIABLES epoch, claim, claimEpoch, slotState, submitted
vars == <<epoch, claim, claimEpoch, slotState, submitted>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ claim \in [Orders -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ claimEpoch \in [Orders -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ slotState \in [Slots -> {"open", "taken"}]
    /\ submitted \subseteq Orders

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ claim = [o \in Orders |-> NoSlot]
    /\ claimEpoch = [o \in Orders |-> 0]
    /\ slotState = [s \in Slots |-> "open"]
    /\ submitted = {}

\* A (possibly slow) order arrives into the auction book; it is never lost.
Submit(o) ==
    /\ o \notin submitted
    /\ submitted' = submitted \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, claim, claimEpoch, slotState>>

\* An unassigned submitted order is filled into an open price-time slot,
\* stamping the fill with the current auction epoch.
Fill(o, s) ==
    /\ o \in submitted
    /\ claim[o] = NoSlot
    /\ slotState[s] = "open"
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![o] = s]
    /\ claimEpoch' = [claimEpoch EXCEPT ![o] = epoch]
    /\ slotState' = [slotState EXCEPT ![s] = "taken"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, submitted>>

\* An order withdraws its current-epoch fill, reopening the slot.
Withdraw(o, s) ==
    /\ claim[o] = s
    /\ claimEpoch[o] = epoch
    /\ slotState[s] = "taken"
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![o] = NoSlot]
    /\ slotState' = [slotState EXCEPT ![s] = "open"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, claimEpoch, submitted>>

\* The auction reopens under a new epoch; all slots become open again.
Reopen ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ slotState' = [s \in Slots |-> "open"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, claimEpoch, submitted>>

Done ==
    /\ \A o \in Orders : o \in submitted
    /\ epoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ \A o \in Orders : claim[o] # NoSlot

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Orders : Submit(o)
    \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Slots : Fill(o, s)
    \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Slots : Withdraw(o, s)
    \/ Reopen
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No slot is double-allocated within a single auction epoch: two orders
\* holding the same slot with the same fill epoch must be the same order.
NoDoubleFill ==
    \A o1 \in Orders, o2 \in Orders :
        (claim[o1] # NoSlot /\ claim[o1] = claim[o2] /\ claimEpoch[o1] = claimEpoch[o2])
            => (o1 = o2)
====
nl: A stock exchange opening auction allocates price-time fill slots to incoming orders across epoch-numbered auction rounds. Participants can be slow but never fail, so every order eventually arrives and is never lost or aborted. In the Submit action a (possibly slow) order arrives into the auction book. In the Fill action an unassigned submitted order is matched into an open slot, and the fill is stamped with the current auction epoch. In the Withdraw action an order that filled a slot in the current epoch pulls its order, reopening that slot for reallocation in the same round. In the Reopen action the auction advances to a new epoch and every slot becomes open again, so a slot filled in an earlier round may be filled by a different order in the new round without conflict. SAFETY PROPERTY: within any single auction epoch no slot is ever held by two different orders, because two orders recorded against the same slot with the same fill epoch must be the same order.

---- MODULE W4Od13m3p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Machine == {1, 2, 3}
MsgId == {1, 2}
Total == 2
MaxTerm == 2
VARIABLES leader, holds, msg, up, term

RECURSIVE SumSet(_, _)
SumSet(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SumSet(f, S \ {x})

InTransit == {i \in MsgId : msg[i] # 0}
HeldTotal == SumSet(holds, Machine)

Init ==
    /\ leader = 0
    /\ holds = [m \in Machine |-> IF m = 1 THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ msg = [i \in MsgId |-> 0]
    /\ up = Machine
    /\ term = 0

\* A live machine takes leadership when the seat is vacant or the leader has died.
Elect(m) ==
    /\ m \in up
    /\ (leader = 0 \/ leader \notin up)
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = m
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, msg, up>>

\* A machine crashes silently; if it was leader the seat is vacated. Keep one alive.
Crash(m) ==
    /\ m \in up
    /\ Cardinality(up) > 1
    /\ up' = up \ {m}
    /\ leader' = (IF leader = m THEN 0 ELSE leader)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, msg, term>>

\* The current leader authorizes moving one token from m into a transit slot bound for d.
Send(m, i, d) ==
    /\ leader # 0
    /\ holds[m] > 0
    /\ msg[i] = 0
    /\ d # m
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
    /\ msg' = [msg EXCEPT ![i] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term>>

\* An in-transit token is delivered; slots may be delivered in any order (reordering).
Deliver(i) ==
    /\ msg[i] # 0
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![msg[i]] = @ + 1]
    /\ msg' = [msg EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, term>>

Done == leader = 0 /\ term = MaxTerm /\ InTransit = {}

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Machine : Elect(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machine : Crash(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machine, i \in MsgId, d \in Machine : Send(m, i, d)
    \/ \E i \in MsgId : Deliver(i)
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, holds, msg, up, term>>)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leader, holds, msg, up, term>>

\* No token is ever created or destroyed: held tokens plus in-flight tokens stay constant.
Conserve == HeldTotal + Cardinality(InTransit) = Total

====
nl:
A network of vending machines shares a pool of tokens and elects a coordinator to authorize token transfers between machines. The seat of leadership starts vacant. Elect lets a live machine claim leadership whenever the seat is empty or the sitting leader has failed, bumping the election term. Crash removes a live machine silently, vacating the seat if that machine was the leader, while always leaving at least one machine alive. Send is authorized by the current leader and moves a single token out of any machine that holds one, alive or crashed, into a transit slot addressed to another machine, so the leader can reclaim tokens from a failed node. Deliver takes an in-transit token from any slot and credits it to its destination; because slots can be delivered in any order, messages may be reordered. When the seat is permanently vacant at the final term and no tokens remain in transit, the system idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of tokens held by machines plus the number of tokens in transit always equals the fixed total, so no token is ever created or destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od5m1p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Player == {1, 2, 3}
Slot == {1, 2}

VARIABLES token, owner, held, want, slow

NextP(p) == IF p = 3 THEN 1 ELSE p + 1

Init ==
    /\ token = 1
    /\ owner = [s \in Slot |-> 0]
    /\ held = [p \in Player |-> {}]
    /\ want = [p \in Player |-> FALSE]
    /\ slow = 0

\* A player currently without any slot signals that it wants to be matched.
Request(p) ==
    /\ ~want[p]
    /\ held[p] = {}
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, owner, held, slow>>

\* Only the token holder may claim a free slot; the ring enforces exclusive access.
Grant(s) ==
    /\ want[token]
    /\ owner[s] = 0
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = token]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![token] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![token] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, slow>>

\* A player relinquishes a slot it holds, returning it to the free pool.
Release(p, s) ==
    /\ s \in held[p]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![p] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, want, slow>>

\* The token advances around the ring, but a currently-slow holder keeps it.
Pass ==
    /\ token # slow
    /\ token' = NextP(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, held, want, slow>>

\* The lobby marks a different player as the slow one (or clears it with 0); nobody fails.
SetSlow(q) ==
    /\ q # slow
    /\ slow' = q
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, owner, held, want>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Player : Request(p)
    \/ \E s \in Slot : Grant(s)
    \/ \E p \in Player, s \in Slot : Release(p, s)
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E q \in Player \cup {0} : SetSlow(q)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<token, owner, held, want, slow>>

\* A slot appears in a player's held view only if that player is its recorded owner,
\* so the same slot can never be allocated to two players at once.
Coherent == \A p \in Player, s \in Slot : (s \in held[p]) => (owner[s] = p)

====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players into a small pool of game slots, using a token that circulates around a ring so that only the token holder may grab a slot. Request lets a player that currently holds no slot announce that it wants to be matched. Grant fires only for the current token holder: if it wants a slot and some slot is free, that slot is assigned to it and recorded both in the authoritative owner map and in the holder's own held view. Release lets any player give up a slot it holds, returning the slot to the free pool. Pass advances the token to the next player around the ring, except that a player currently flagged as slow keeps the token instead of forwarding it. SetSlow changes which single player is flagged slow, or clears the flag with 0, modeling that a participant can lag but never crashes. Because slot claims only ever happen for the lone token holder against a free slot, two players can never wind up holding the same slot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A slot is listed in a player's held view only when that player is the slot's recorded owner, so no slot is ever allocated to two players simultaneously.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m7p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Router == {1, 2}
Bag == {1, 2}

VARIABLES reg, loaded, rd, expd, slow

Init ==
    /\ reg = [b \in Bag |-> 0]
    /\ loaded = [b \in Bag |-> 0]
    /\ rd = [r \in Router |-> 0]
    /\ expd = [r \in Router |-> 0]
    /\ slow = 0

\* A router snapshots a bag's claim register; a slow router may act on this later when stale.
Read(r, b) ==
    /\ rd' = [rd EXCEPT ![r] = b]
    /\ expd' = [expd EXCEPT ![r] = reg[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, loaded, slow>>

\* Compare-and-swap: the claim only lands if the register still equals the snapshot read.
Claim(r) ==
    /\ r # slow
    /\ rd[r] # 0
    /\ loaded[rd[r]] = 0
    /\ reg[rd[r]] = expd[r]
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![rd[r]] = r]
    /\ rd' = [rd EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loaded, expd, slow>>

\* The irreversible load: only the router that owns the bag's register may load it onto a plane.
Load(r, b) ==
    /\ reg[b] = r
    /\ loaded[b] = 0
    /\ loaded' = [loaded EXCEPT ![b] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, rd, expd, slow>>

\* A router that owns a not-yet-loaded bag may drop its claim so others can contend.
Release(r, b) ==
    /\ reg[b] = r
    /\ loaded[b] = 0
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loaded, rd, expd, slow>>

\* The router that is currently lagging changes; participants slow down but never crash.
SetSlow(q) ==
    /\ q # slow
    /\ slow' = q
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, loaded, rd, expd>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Router, b \in Bag : Read(r, b)
    \/ \E r \in Router : Claim(r)
    \/ \E r \in Router, b \in Bag : Load(r, b)
    \/ \E r \in Router, b \in Bag : Release(r, b)
    \/ \E q \in Router \cup {0} : SetSlow(q)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, loaded, rd, expd, slow>>

\* Once a bag has been irreversibly loaded, its claim register is frozen to the very router
\* that loaded it, so no second router can ever load the same bag.
LoadCoherent == \A b \in Bag : loaded[b] # 0 => reg[b] = loaded[b]

====
nl:
An airport baggage router uses a per-bag compare-and-swap claim register to decide which sorting router gets to load each bag onto its plane, an action that cannot be undone once done. Read lets a router snapshot the current value of a bag's claim register into its own scratch fields; a slow router may keep acting on this snapshot after it has gone stale. Claim is the compare-and-swap itself: a router installs itself as the register's owner only if the register still equals the value it snapshotted and the bag is not already loaded, so a lagging router with a stale snapshot simply fails to claim. Load is the irreversible step, permitted only for the router that currently owns the bag's register and only if the bag has not yet been loaded, after which the bag is recorded as loaded by that router. Release lets a router that owns a still-unloaded bag drop its claim so other routers can contend for it. SetSlow changes which single router is currently lagging, capturing that a participant can be slow but never fails outright. Because loading freezes the register and no one can re-claim or release a loaded bag, each bag is loaded by exactly one router at most once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Once a bag has been loaded, its claim register stays fixed to the exact router that loaded it, so the same bag can never be loaded by a second router.

---- MODULE W4Od9m0p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Controller == {1, 2}
Feeder == {1, 2}
MaxVer == 3

VARIABLES ver, shed, tripper, snap, crashed, cver

Init ==
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ shed = [f \in Feeder |-> FALSE]
    /\ tripper = [f \in Feeder |-> 0]
    /\ snap = [c \in Controller |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = 0
    /\ cver = [f \in Feeder |-> 0]

\* A live controller (re-)reads the grid config version into its optimistic snapshot; this is
\* both the initial read and the retry after a failed validation.
ReadVer(c) ==
    /\ c # crashed
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, shed, tripper, crashed, cver>>

\* Some rebalancing bumps the shared config version, invalidating stale snapshots (forcing retry).
Reconfig(c) ==
    /\ c # crashed
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shed, tripper, snap, crashed, cver>>

\* The irreversible shed: a controller trips a feeder only if its snapshot still matches the live
\* version (optimistic validation) and the feeder is not already shed; committing consumes the
\* version by recording it and bumping the shared version so concurrent stale writers must retry.
Shed(c, f) ==
    /\ c # crashed
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ snap[c] = ver
    /\ ~shed[f]
    /\ shed' = [shed EXCEPT ![f] = TRUE]
    /\ tripper' = [tripper EXCEPT ![f] = c]
    /\ cver' = [cver EXCEPT ![f] = ver]
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, crashed>>

\* At most one controller may crash silently, after which it takes no further action.
Crash(c) ==
    /\ crashed = 0
    /\ crashed' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, shed, tripper, snap, cver>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controller : ReadVer(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controller : Reconfig(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controller, f \in Feeder : Shed(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Controller : Crash(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<ver, shed, tripper, snap, crashed, cver>>

\* Each config version authorizes at most one irreversible shed: two shed feeders that were
\* committed against the same version must in fact be the same feeder.
CommitUnique ==
    \A f1, f2 \in Feeder :
        (shed[f1] /\ shed[f2] /\ cver[f1] = cver[f2]) => f1 = f2

====
nl:
A power-grid load shedder lets several controllers race to trip feeders under optimistic locking: each controller reads a shared config version, decides locally, and only commits a trip if the version has not changed underneath it, otherwise it retries. ReadVer lets a live controller take (or refresh) its optimistic snapshot of the current config version, serving as both the first read and the retry after a validation failure. Reconfig models background rebalancing that bumps the shared config version, invalidating any stale snapshots so their holders must retry. Shed is the irreversible trip: a live controller disconnects a feeder only when its snapshot still equals the live version and the feeder is not already shed; committing records the tripping controller and the exact version consumed, then bumps the shared version so a concurrent controller holding the old snapshot is forced to retry rather than commit a lost update. Crash lets at most one controller fail silently, after which it never acts again. Because every successful trip consumes and advances the version, two different feeders can never be shed on the strength of the same config version.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every config version authorizes at most one irreversible feeder trip, so two distinct shed feeders can never share the same committed version.

---- MODULE W4Od19m8p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Patron == {1, 2}
Book == {1, 2, 3, 4}
Branch == {1, 2}
Cap == 2

\* Books 1..3 live at branch 1; book 4 lives at branch 2 (the coarse/fine hierarchy).
BranchOf(b) == IF b <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 2

VARIABLES branchLock, bookRes, open, crashed

ReservedCount(B) == Cardinality({b \in Book : BranchOf(b) = B /\ bookRes[b] # 0})

Init ==
    /\ branchLock = [B \in Branch |-> 0]
    /\ bookRes = [b \in Book |-> 0]
    /\ open = [B \in Branch |-> TRUE]
    /\ crashed = 0

\* A branch opens or closes for service; this is always possible and keeps the system live.
Toggle(B) ==
    /\ open' = [open EXCEPT ![B] = ~open[B]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branchLock, bookRes, crashed>>

\* Coarse lock: a live patron takes the branch-level lock, only while the branch is open.
AcquireBranch(p, B) ==
    /\ p # crashed
    /\ open[B]
    /\ branchLock[B] = 0
    /\ branchLock' = [branchLock EXCEPT ![B] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookRes, open, crashed>>

\* Fine lock: holding the branch lock, a patron reserves a free book, but only if the branch
\* still has spare reservation capacity.
Reserve(p, b) ==
    /\ p # crashed
    /\ branchLock[BranchOf(b)] = p
    /\ bookRes[b] = 0
    /\ ReservedCount(BranchOf(b)) < Cap
    /\ bookRes' = [bookRes EXCEPT ![b] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branchLock, open, crashed>>

\* A patron holding the branch lock cancels one of its own reservations, freeing capacity.
Cancel(p, b) ==
    /\ p # crashed
    /\ branchLock[BranchOf(b)] = p
    /\ bookRes[b] = p
    /\ bookRes' = [bookRes EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branchLock, open, crashed>>

\* Releasing the coarse lock so another patron may take the branch.
ReleaseBranch(p, B) ==
    /\ p # crashed
    /\ branchLock[B] = p
    /\ branchLock' = [branchLock EXCEPT ![B] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookRes, open, crashed>>

\* At most one patron crashes silently; its held locks and reservations simply linger.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ crashed = 0
    /\ crashed' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branchLock, bookRes, open>>

Next ==
    \/ \E B \in Branch : Toggle(B)
    \/ \E p \in Patron, B \in Branch : AcquireBranch(p, B)
    \/ \E p \in Patron, b \in Book : Reserve(p, b)
    \/ \E p \in Patron, b \in Book : Cancel(p, b)
    \/ \E p \in Patron, B \in Branch : ReleaseBranch(p, B)
    \/ \E p \in Patron : Crash(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<branchLock, bookRes, open, crashed>>

\* No branch ever holds more active reservations than its fixed capacity.
Capacity == \A B \in Branch : ReservedCount(B) <= Cap

====
nl:
A library book reservation system guards each branch with a coarse branch-level lock that a patron must take before touching any individual book (the fine level) in that branch, so reservations are made hierarchically, coarse lock then fine reservation. Toggle opens or closes a branch for service and is always available, keeping the system live. AcquireBranch lets a live patron take the coarse lock on an open, unlocked branch. Reserve is the fine-grained step: while holding the branch's coarse lock, a patron reserves a currently free book, but only when that branch still has spare capacity below its fixed limit. Cancel lets a patron holding the branch lock drop one of its own reservations, returning capacity to the branch. ReleaseBranch gives up the coarse lock so another patron can take the branch. Crash lets at most one patron fail silently, leaving its locks and reservations lingering, while the surviving patron keeps operating. Because every reservation is made under the branch lock and only when capacity remains, a branch's active reservations never exceed its limit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No branch ever holds more active book reservations than its fixed capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m7p5t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Slot      == {1, 2, 3}
Instance  == {"a", "b"}
Free      == "free"
None      == "none"

VARIABLES reg, committed, cBy, holding

vars == <<reg, committed, cBy, holding>>

Init ==
    /\ reg       = [s \in Slot |-> Free]
    /\ committed = [s \in Slot |-> FALSE]
    /\ cBy       = [s \in Slot |-> None]
    /\ holding   = [i \in Instance |-> 0]

\* Compare-and-swap acquire: only succeeds from Free, and the caller must be idle.
Acquire(i, s) ==
    /\ holding[i] = 0
    /\ reg[s] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = i]
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![i] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, cBy>>

\* The one-time irreversible landing on a held runway.
Commit(i, s) ==
    /\ holding[i] = s
    /\ reg[s] = i
    /\ committed[s] = FALSE
    /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ cBy' = [cBy EXCEPT ![s] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, holding>>

\* Abort before landing: CAS the register back to Free and go idle.
Release(i, s) ==
    /\ holding[i] = s
    /\ reg[s] = i
    /\ committed[s] = FALSE
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, cBy>>

\* Step away after a landing; ownership of the committed slot is retained.
Finish(i, s) ==
    /\ holding[i] = s
    /\ reg[s] = i
    /\ committed[s] = TRUE
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, committed, cBy>>

Done == \A s \in Slot : committed[s]

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instance, s \in Slot :
         \/ Acquire(i, s)
         \/ Commit(i, s)
         \/ Release(i, s)
         \/ Finish(i, s)
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A landed runway keeps a fixed owner in both the record and the CAS register.
Safety ==
    \A s \in Slot :
        committed[s] => /\ cBy[s] \in Instance
                        /\ reg[s] = cBy[s]

=============================================================================
nl: Two independent air-traffic allocator instances, "a" and "b", share one pool of three runways. Each runway carries a compare-and-swap register that is either Free or names the owning instance. An idle instance performs Acquire on a Free runway, atomically swapping the register from Free to itself and recording the runway in its holding slot. Once it owns a runway an instance may perform Commit, the irreversible landing, which flips the runway's committed flag to TRUE exactly once and stamps the landing instance into cBy. Before landing, an instance may instead perform Release, compare-and-swapping the register back to Free and going idle so the shared runway returns to the pool. After a landing an instance performs Finish, going idle while deliberately retaining ownership of the committed runway so it can never be reclaimed. SAFETY PROPERTY: Every runway that has been landed retains a fixed landing instance recorded in cBy that still matches the runway's compare-and-swap register.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m2p6t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

P        == {"r1", "r2", "r3"}
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES epoch, phase, voted, ballot, decision, applied

vars == <<epoch, phase, voted, ballot, decision, applied>>

Init ==
    /\ epoch    = 0
    /\ phase    = "decided"
    /\ voted    = [p \in P |-> 0]
    /\ ballot   = [p \in P |-> "none"]
    /\ decision = "none"
    /\ applied  = [p \in P |-> 0]

\* Coordinator opens a fresh round, invalidating every prior-round artifact.
StartRound ==
    /\ phase = "decided"
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch'    = epoch + 1
    /\ phase'    = "collect"
    /\ voted'    = [p \in P |-> 0]
    /\ ballot'   = [p \in P |-> "none"]
    /\ decision' = "none"
    /\ applied'  = [p \in P |-> 0]

\* A (possibly slow) participant casts a vote stamped with the live epoch.
Vote(p, v) ==
    /\ phase = "collect"
    /\ voted[p] < epoch
    /\ voted'  = [voted  EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![p] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, phase, decision, applied>>

\* Coordinator resolves once every participant has voted in this epoch.
Decide ==
    /\ phase = "collect"
    /\ \A p \in P : voted[p] = epoch
    /\ decision' = IF \A p \in P : ballot[p] = "yes" THEN "commit" ELSE "abort"
    /\ phase'    = "decided"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, voted, ballot, applied>>

\* A participant enacts the decision only if it voted this very epoch.
Apply(p) ==
    /\ phase = "decided"
    /\ decision # "none"
    /\ applied[p] < epoch
    /\ voted[p] = epoch
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, phase, voted, ballot, decision>>

Done ==
    /\ phase = "decided"
    /\ epoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ \A p \in P : applied[p] = epoch

Next ==
    \/ StartRound
    \/ \E p \in P, v \in {"yes", "no"} : Vote(p, v)
    \/ Decide
    \/ \E p \in P : Apply(p)
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Any enacted decision was made this epoch by a participant that voted this epoch.
Safety ==
    \A p \in P :
        applied[p] # 0 =>
            /\ decision # "none"
            /\ applied[p] = epoch
            /\ voted[p] = epoch

=============================================================================
nl: A warehouse robot fleet of three participant robots commits shared tasks under a coordinator using two-phase commit, and because a robot may be slow but never fails, the coordinator stamps every round with an epoch number to fence out stale messages. StartRound opens a fresh commit round: the coordinator increments the epoch, clears all votes, ballots, the decision, and every participant's applied stamp. Vote lets a possibly-slow robot cast a "yes" or "no" ballot stamped with the currently live epoch. Decide fires once every robot has voted in the current epoch, resolving to commit if all ballots are yes and to abort otherwise. Apply lets a robot enact the decision, but only if that robot actually voted in this same epoch, so a stale or unauthorized robot from an earlier round cannot act. SAFETY PROPERTY: Any robot that has enacted the decision did so at the current epoch and had itself voted in that same epoch on a coordinator decision that exists.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m1p5t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

Node   == {1, 2, 3}
Course == {"c1", "c2"}
NoNode == 0

Nxt(n) == (n % 3) + 1

VARIABLES token, crashed, reservation, enrolled, enrolledBy

vars == <<token, crashed, reservation, enrolled, enrolledBy>>

Init ==
    /\ token       = 1
    /\ crashed     = [n \in Node |-> FALSE]
    /\ reservation = [c \in Course |-> NoNode]
    /\ enrolled    = [c \in Course |-> FALSE]
    /\ enrolledBy  = [c \in Course |-> NoNode]

\* The live token holder hands exclusive access to the next node on the ring.
PassToken ==
    /\ ~crashed[token]
    /\ token' = Nxt(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, reservation, enrolled, enrolledBy>>

\* Exactly one registrar may crash silently, and only if none has yet.
Crash(n) ==
    /\ \A m \in Node : ~crashed[m]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, reservation, enrolled, enrolledBy>>

\* The token holder tentatively reserves a still-open course seat.
Reserve(n, c) ==
    /\ token = n
    /\ ~crashed[n]
    /\ enrolled[c] = FALSE
    /\ reservation[c] = NoNode
    /\ reservation' = [reservation EXCEPT ![c] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, crashed, enrolled, enrolledBy>>

\* The token holder finalizes its own reservation: the one-time enrollment.
Enroll(n, c) ==
    /\ token = n
    /\ ~crashed[n]
    /\ enrolled[c] = FALSE
    /\ reservation[c] = n
    /\ enrolled'   = [enrolled   EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ enrolledBy' = [enrolledBy EXCEPT ![c] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, crashed, reservation>>

Done == crashed[token]

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E n \in Node : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Node, c \in Course : Reserve(n, c)
    \/ \E n \in Node, c \in Course : Enroll(n, c)
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A finalized course carries a fixed finalizer that matches its held reservation.
Safety ==
    \A c \in Course :
        enrolled[c] => /\ enrolledBy[c] \in Node
                       /\ reservation[c] = enrolledBy[c]

=============================================================================
nl: A university course-registration system grants exclusive access to shared course seats by circulating a single token around a ring of three registrar nodes, where one node may crash silently at any point. PassToken lets the live token holder hand exclusive access to the next node clockwise on the ring. Crash permits exactly one registrar to fail silently, and only while no node has yet crashed; a crashed node can no longer pass the token or act, so the ring may stall on it. Reserve lets the current token holder place a tentative reservation on a course seat that is still open and unreserved. Enroll lets that same token holder finalize its own reservation, the one-time irreversible enrollment that flips the course's enrolled flag and stamps the finalizing node, and it can never fire twice for a course. SAFETY PROPERTY: Every finalized course records a real finalizing node that matches the node holding that course's reservation.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m2p4t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

Fridge   == {"f1", "f2"}
TotalCap == 4
MaxDep   == 2

VARIABLES stock, reserved, phase, votes, pending

vars == <<stock, reserved, phase, votes, pending>>

Used == stock["f1"] + stock["f2"] + reserved["f1"] + reserved["f2"]

Init ==
    /\ stock    = [f \in Fridge |-> 0]
    /\ reserved = [f \in Fridge |-> 0]
    /\ phase    = "idle"
    /\ votes    = [f \in Fridge |-> "none"]
    /\ pending  = [f \in Fridge |-> 0]

\* Coordinator proposes a fresh cross-fridge deposit transaction.
Propose ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ \E amt \in [Fridge -> 0..MaxDep] :
         pending' = amt
    /\ phase'    = "voting"
    /\ votes'    = [f \in Fridge |-> "none"]
    /\ reserved' = [f \in Fridge |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED stock

\* A (possibly slow) fridge votes yes and reserves only if the bank-wide
\* capacity still admits its share, else it votes no.
Vote(f) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[f] = "none"
    /\ LET fits == Used + pending[f] <= TotalCap IN
         /\ votes'    = [votes    EXCEPT ![f] = IF fits THEN "yes" ELSE "no"]
         /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![f] = IF fits THEN pending[f] ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, phase, pending>>

\* Coordinator commits only under unanimous yes.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A f \in Fridge : votes[f] = "yes"
    /\ phase' = "committing"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, reserved, votes, pending>>

\* Any no vote aborts, discarding all reservations.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E f \in Fridge : votes[f] = "no"
    /\ phase'    = "idle"
    /\ reserved' = [f \in Fridge |-> 0]
    /\ pending'  = [f \in Fridge |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, votes>>

\* A participant enacts its reserved deposit into committed stock.
Apply(f) ==
    /\ phase = "committing"
    /\ reserved[f] > 0
    /\ stock'    = [stock    EXCEPT ![f] = stock[f] + reserved[f]]
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![f] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, pending>>

\* Transaction closes once every reservation is enacted.
Finish ==
    /\ phase = "committing"
    /\ \A f \in Fridge : reserved[f] = 0
    /\ phase'   = "idle"
    /\ pending' = [f \in Fridge |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, reserved, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ Propose
    \/ \E f \in Fridge : Vote(f)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E f \in Fridge : Apply(f)
    \/ Finish

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Committed plus reserved units never exceed the bank's total capacity.
Safety == Used <= TotalCap

=============================================================================
nl: A blood-bank inventory tracker coordinates cross-fridge deposit transactions across two fridge participants using two-phase commit, where a fridge may be slow to respond but never fails, and the bank enforces one shared total storage capacity. Propose opens a transaction by choosing how many units are proposed for each fridge. Vote lets a possibly-slow fridge respond: it votes yes and tentatively reserves its proposed units only when the bank-wide committed-plus-reserved total still admits that share, and otherwise votes no and reserves nothing. Commit advances the transaction only under a unanimous yes. Abort discards all reservations the moment any fridge votes no. Apply enacts a fridge's reserved units into its committed stock. Finish closes the transaction once every reservation has been enacted. SAFETY PROPERTY: The bank's committed stock plus all outstanding reservations never exceeds its total capacity.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m3p5t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

Node    == {1, 2, 3}
MaxTerm == 3

VARIABLES term, leader, msgs, unlocked, unlockTerm

vars == <<term, leader, msgs, unlocked, unlockTerm>>

Init ==
    /\ term       = 1
    /\ leader     = 1
    /\ msgs       = {}
    /\ unlocked   = FALSE
    /\ unlockTerm = 0

\* Failover: a new term promotes a fresh leader. Elections halt once unlocked.
Elect(n) ==
    /\ ~unlocked
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term'   = term + 1
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<msgs, unlocked, unlockTerm>>

\* The reigning leader emits a commit message stamped with its term; it may
\* then linger and be delivered out of order relative to later elections.
SendCommit ==
    /\ ~unlocked
    /\ ~\E m \in msgs : m.t = term
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[t |-> term, n |-> leader]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, unlocked, unlockTerm>>

\* A delivered commit fires the one-time unlock only if it is still current.
Deliver ==
    /\ ~unlocked
    /\ \E m \in msgs :
         /\ m.t = term
         /\ unlocked'   = TRUE
         /\ unlockTerm' = term
         /\ msgs'       = msgs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader>>

\* A superseded (or post-unlock) message is discarded from the network.
DropMsg ==
    /\ \E m \in msgs :
         /\ (m.t < term \/ unlocked)
         /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, unlocked, unlockTerm>>

Done == unlocked /\ msgs = {}

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Node : Elect(n)
    \/ SendCommit
    \/ Deliver
    \/ DropMsg
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* If the master unlock has fired, it fired under the still-reigning term,
\* so no stale reordered message from a superseded term ever triggered it.
Safety == unlocked => unlockTerm = term

=============================================================================
nl: A smart-home door-lock network elects a coordinating leader across terms with failover, and the one-time master unlock must fire at most once even though commit messages can be reordered and delivered late. Elect performs a failover, advancing to a new term and promoting a fresh leader node, and elections halt permanently once the door is unlocked. SendCommit lets the reigning leader emit a commit message stamped with its current term; that message may then linger in the network and be delivered out of order relative to later elections. Deliver fires the one-time master unlock, but only when the delivered message's term still matches the currently reigning term, so a stale message from a superseded leader is refused. DropMsg discards a message that has been superseded by a higher term or that remains after the unlock has already fired. SAFETY PROPERTY: If the master unlock has fired, it fired under the term that is still reigning, so no stale reordered message from a superseded term ever triggered it.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m8p0t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

Robot == {1, 2, 3}
CapValues == 0..2

VARIABLES coarse, fine, phase, cap

vars == <<coarse, fine, phase, cap>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Robot \cup {0}
    /\ fine \in Robot \cup {0}
    /\ phase \in [Robot -> {"idle", "coarse", "fine"}]
    /\ cap \in CapValues

Init ==
    /\ coarse = 0
    /\ fine = 0
    /\ phase = [r \in Robot |-> "idle"]
    /\ cap = 2

\* Acquire the coarse (zone) lock first.
AcquireCoarse(r) ==
    /\ coarse = 0
    /\ phase[r] = "idle"
    /\ coarse' = r
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "coarse"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, cap>>

\* Only a robot already holding the coarse lock may take the fine lock,
\* and only if the runtime capacity currently permits it.
AcquireFine(r) ==
    /\ coarse = r
    /\ fine = 0
    /\ phase[r] = "coarse"
    /\ cap > 0
    /\ fine' = r
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "fine"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, cap>>

\* Release the fine lock, dropping back to holding only the coarse lock.
ReleaseFine(r) ==
    /\ fine = r
    /\ fine' = 0
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "coarse"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, cap>>

\* Release the coarse lock once the fine lock is no longer held by us.
ReleaseCoarse(r) ==
    /\ coarse = r
    /\ fine # r
    /\ coarse' = 0
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, cap>>

\* The critical resource's capacity is reconfigured while the fleet runs.
ChangeCapacity ==
    /\ \E c \in CapValues : c # cap /\ cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, phase>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robot : AcquireCoarse(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robot : AcquireFine(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robot : ReleaseFine(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robot : ReleaseCoarse(r)
    \/ ChangeCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A robot in the critical (fine) phase must genuinely own both the coarse
\* and the fine lock; since the fine lock is single-valued this enforces
\* mutual exclusion of the critical resource.
MutexCoherent ==
    \A r \in Robot :
        phase[r] = "fine" => (fine = r /\ coarse = r)

========================================================================
nl: A fleet of warehouse robots contends for a single critical resource that is protected by a two-level hierarchical lock: a coarse zone lock that must be taken before the fine resource lock. A robot first runs AcquireCoarse to grab the zone lock when it is free, moving from idle to holding the coarse lock. It then runs AcquireFine to take the fine lock, but only if it already holds the coarse lock and the resource's runtime capacity is currently positive. ReleaseFine drops the fine lock back to the coarse-only state, and ReleaseCoarse gives up the zone lock once the robot no longer holds the fine lock, returning to idle. Meanwhile ChangeCapacity models the critical resource's capacity being reconfigured to a different value at runtime, which can gate future fine acquisitions. Because the fine lock is single-valued, only one robot can ever be in the critical section at a time. MaxWrites == 2

vars == <<ver, log, view, adminMode>>

AdminId == 0
Writer == Robot \cup {AdminId}

    /\ ver \in 0..MaxWrites
    /\ ver = Len(log)
    /\ view \in [Robot -> 0..MaxWrites]
    /\ adminMode \in BOOLEAN
    /\ \A i \in DOMAIN log :
           /\ log[i].who \in Writer

    /\ ver = 0
    /\ log = << >>
    /\ view = [r \in Robot |-> 0]

\* A robot reads the current version of the register into its local view.
Read(r) ==
    /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![r] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, log, adminMode>>

\* Compare-and-swap: a robot may commit a write only if the version it last
\* read still matches the register's current version (it is authorized and
\* not stale). The write records the version the robot claims to have seen.
CAS(r) ==
    /\ ver < MaxWrites
    /\ view[r] = ver
    /\ log' = Append(log, [who |-> r, saw |-> view[r]])
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<view, adminMode>>

\* Privileged admin override: when admin mode is armed, a forced write is
\* committed regardless of any robot's view.
AdminOverride ==
    /\ adminMode
    /\ ver < MaxWrites
    /\ log' = Append(log, [who |-> AdminId, saw |-> ver])
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<view, adminMode>>

\* Arm or disarm the privileged admin override.
ToggleAdmin ==
    /\ adminMode' = ~adminMode
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, log, view>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robot : Read(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robot : CAS(r)
    \/ AdminOverride
    \/ ToggleAdmin

\* Every committed write in the log was either an admin override or was made
\* by a robot that saw the immediately preceding version -- so no stale or
\* unauthorized robot write ever lands in the log.

    \A i \in DOMAIN log :
        log[i].who = AdminId \/ log[i].saw = i - 1

Read lets a robot copy the register's current version into its own local view. CAS is the compare-and-swap commit: a robot may append a write to the register's log and advance the version only if the version it last read still equals the register's current version, which means the robot is authorized and not acting on stale data; the recorded write remembers the version the robot claims to have seen. The twist is a privileged admin override: AdminOverride commits a forced write regardless of any robot's view, but only while admin mode is armed, and ToggleAdmin arms or disarms that privileged mode. The log therefore accumulates a contiguous history of versioned writes.     /\ holds \in [Train -> SUBSET Block]

    /\ alloc = [b \in Block |-> 0]
    /\ holds = [t \in Train |-> {}]

LockRegion(t) ==
    /\ region = 0
    /\ region' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, holds, capacity>>

\* Fine lock: the train holding the region claims a free signal block, but
\* only while the number of occupied blocks is below the live capacity.
AllocBlock(t, b) ==

    /\ alloc[b] = 0
    /\ Cardinality(Allocated) < capacity
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![b] = t]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![t] = holds[t] \cup {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, capacity>>

\* Release a signal block the train currently occupies.
FreeBlock(t, b) ==
    /\ alloc[b] = t
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![t] = holds[t] \ {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, capacity>>

\* Release the coarse region lock once the train holds no blocks.
UnlockRegion(t) ==
    /\ region = t
    /\ holds[t] = {}
    /\ region' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, holds, capacity>>

SetCapacity ==
    /\ \E c \in CapRange : c # capacity /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, alloc, holds>>

    \/ \E t \in Train, b \in Block : FreeBlock(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Train : UnlockRegion(t)
    \/ SetCapacity

\* Every block a train believes it holds is allocated to exactly that train;
\* since alloc gives each block a single owner, no signal block is ever
\* double-allocated to two different trains at once.

Holding the region, the train runs AllocBlock to claim a specific free signal block, but only while the count of currently occupied blocks is still below the system's live capacity. FreeBlock releases a block the train occupies, and UnlockRegion gives up the coarse region lock once the train holds no blocks. The twist is SetCapacity, which reconfigures the number of usable signal blocks at runtime to any different value, tightening or loosening how many blocks may be occupied. Blocks and their owning trains are always kept consistent as locks are taken and released. SAFETY PROPERTY: Every signal block a train holds is allocated to exactly that train, so the same block is never allocated to two different trains simultaneously.

Instance == {"a", "b"}

vars == <<pstate, target, pool, votes, owner>>

    /\ target \in [Instance -> Slot \cup {0}]
    /\ pool \in [Slot -> {"free", "held"}]
    /\ votes \in [Instance -> {"none", "yes"}]
    /\ owner \in [Slot -> Instance \cup {0}]

    /\ pstate = [i \in Instance |-> "idle"]
    /\ target = [i \in Instance |-> 0]
    /\ pool = [s \in Slot |-> "free"]
    /\ votes = [i \in Instance |-> "none"]
    /\ owner = [s \in Slot |-> 0]

\* Coordinator phase 1: an idle instance proposes a chute slot that looks free.
Propose(i, s) ==
    /\ pstate[i] = "idle"
    /\ pool[s] = "free"
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![i] = s]
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![i] = "proposed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, votes, owner>>

\* Participant vote: prepare to grant the slot if it is still free.
Vote(i) ==
    /\ pstate[i] = "proposed"
    /\ pool[target[i]] = "free"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = "yes"]
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![i] = "prepared"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<target, pool, owner>>

\* Coordinator phase 2 (commit): claim the slot, but only if it is STILL free
\* -- the other instance sharing the pool may have grabbed it in between.
Commit(i) ==
    /\ pstate[i] = "prepared"
    /\ votes[i] = "yes"
    /\ pool[target[i]] = "free"
    /\ pool' = [pool EXCEPT ![target[i]] = "held"]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![target[i]] = i]
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![i] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<target, votes>>

\* Abort when the targeted slot was taken by the other instance.
Abort(i) ==
    /\ pstate[i] \in {"proposed", "prepared"}
    /\ pool[target[i]] = "held"
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![i] = "aborted"]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<target, pool, owner>>

\* Release a committed slot back to the shared pool.
Release(i) ==
    /\ pstate[i] = "committed"
    /\ pool' = [pool EXCEPT ![target[i]] = "free"]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![target[i]] = 0]
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes>>

\* An aborted instance resets so it can try another slot.
Reset(i) ==
    /\ pstate[i] = "aborted"
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, votes, owner>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instance, s \in Slot : Propose(i, s)
    \/ \E i \in Instance : Vote(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instance : Commit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instance : Abort(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instance : Release(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instance : Reset(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A committed instance is the recorded owner of the slot it targeted; because
\* each slot records a single owner, two instances sharing the pool can never
\* both commit the same chute slot.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A i \in Instance :
        pstate[i] = "committed" => owner[target[i]] = i

Propose is the coordinator's phase-one step: an idle instance picks a slot that currently looks free and moves to the proposed state. Vote is the participant preparing to grant the slot, transitioning to prepared only if the slot is still free. Commit is phase two, where the instance actually claims the slot and records itself as owner, but it must re-check that the slot is STILL free, because the other instance sharing the pool may have grabbed it in the meantime. Abort fires when a proposed or prepared instance finds its target slot already held by the other instance. Release returns a committed slot to the shared pool and idles the instance, and Reset lets an aborted instance start over on another slot. SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever an instance is committed, it is the sole recorded owner of the slot it targeted, so the two instances never both commit the same chute slot.

Ctrl == {1, 2}
Total == 2
Free == 0

VARIABLES reg, poolTok, lockTok, snap, target, phase

vars == <<reg, poolTok, lockTok, snap, target, phase>>

LockSum == lockTok[1] + lockTok[2] + lockTok[3]

Init ==
    /\ reg = [l \in Locks |-> Free]
    /\ poolTok = Total
    /\ lockTok = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ snap = [c \in Ctrl |-> Free]
    /\ target = [c \in Ctrl |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [c \in Ctrl |-> "idle"]

Read(c, l) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "idle"
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = reg[l]]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![c] = l]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "attempting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, poolTok, lockTok>>

CASAcquire(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "attempting"
    /\ reg[target[c]] = snap[c]
    /\ reg[target[c]] = Free
    /\ poolTok > 0
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![target[c]] = c]
    /\ poolTok' = poolTok - 1
    /\ lockTok' = [lockTok EXCEPT ![target[c]] = lockTok[target[c]] + 1]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, target>>

CASFail(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "attempting"
    /\ reg[target[c]] # snap[c]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, poolTok, lockTok, snap, target>>

Release(c, l) ==
    /\ reg[l] = c
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![l] = Free]
    /\ poolTok' = poolTok + 1
    /\ lockTok' = [lockTok EXCEPT ![l] = lockTok[l] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, target, phase>>

Transfer(c, l1, l2) ==
    /\ l1 # l2
    /\ reg[l1] = c
    /\ reg[l2] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![l1] = Free, ![l2] = c]
    /\ lockTok' = [lockTok EXCEPT ![l1] = lockTok[l1] - 1, ![l2] = lockTok[l2] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<poolTok, snap, target, phase>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl, l \in Locks : Read(c, l)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl : CASAcquire(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl : CASFail(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl, l \in Locks : Release(c, l)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl, l1 \in Locks, l2 \in Locks : Transfer(c, l1, l2)

A controller runs Read to snapshot the current owner-register value of some lock and enter an attempting phase. It then runs CASAcquire, which succeeds only if the register still equals the snapshot and the lock is free and the pool has a spare token: it swaps the register to name this controller and moves one token from the shared pool onto that lock. If instead the register no longer matches the snapshot, CASFail abandons the attempt and returns the controller to idle. A controller that owns a lock runs Release to set the register back to free and return the lock's token to the shared pool, or runs Transfer to atomically move ownership and the token from one lock it holds to another free lock without touching the pool. Items == {1, 2}
Quorum == 2
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES epoch, bankEpoch, voteEp, settled, authEp

vars == <<epoch, bankEpoch, voteEp, settled, authEp>>

CurrentVotes(it) == {p \in Banks : voteEp[it][p] = epoch}
AuthVotes(it) == {p \in Banks : voteEp[it][p] = authEp[it]}

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 1
    /\ bankEpoch = [p \in Banks |-> 1]
    /\ voteEp = [it \in Items |-> [p \in Banks |-> 0]]
    /\ settled = {}
    /\ authEp = [it \in Items |-> 0]

Reconfig ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bankEpoch, voteEp, settled, authEp>>

Sync(p) ==
    /\ bankEpoch[p] < epoch
    /\ bankEpoch' = [bankEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = bankEpoch[p] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, voteEp, settled, authEp>>

Vote(p, it) ==
    /\ it \notin settled
    /\ voteEp[it][p] # bankEpoch[p]
    /\ voteEp' = [voteEp EXCEPT ![it][p] = bankEpoch[p]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, bankEpoch, settled, authEp>>

Withdraw(p, it) ==
    /\ it \notin settled
    /\ voteEp[it][p] # 0
    /\ voteEp' = [voteEp EXCEPT ![it][p] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, bankEpoch, settled, authEp>>

Settle(it) ==
    /\ it \notin settled
    /\ Cardinality(CurrentVotes(it)) >= Quorum
    /\ settled' = settled \cup {it}
    /\ authEp' = [authEp EXCEPT ![it] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, bankEpoch, voteEp>>

    \/ \E p \in Banks : Sync(p)
    \/ \E p \in Banks, it \in Items : Vote(p, it)
    \/ \E p \in Banks, it \in Items : Withdraw(p, it)
    \/ \E it \in Items : Settle(it)
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

    \A it \in Items :
        it \in settled => Cardinality(AuthVotes(it)) >= Quorum

nl: A consortium of banks clears items in an interbank settlement batch where every settlement action requires a quorum of banks that are voting under the current configuration epoch, so that a stale or unauthorized bank cannot push an action through; a lagging bank may be slow (stuck on an old epoch) but is never failed and can catch up. Sync lets a lagging bank advance its own known epoch one step toward the global epoch, modeling a slow participant catching up rather than failing. A bank runs Vote on an unsettled item, stamping its vote with its own currently-known epoch, and may run Withdraw to retract a vote it previously cast. Settle finalizes an unsettled item only when a quorum of banks have votes stamped with the current global epoch, recording the epoch that authorized it. When all items are settled the batch idles via a terminal self-loop. SAFETY PROPERTY: Every settled item was authorized by at least a quorum of banks whose votes were stamped with that item's own authorizing epoch, so no settlement rests on stale votes.

Cars == {1, 2}
MaxVer == 2

VARIABLES served, version, snapVer, attempt, phase

vars == <<served, version, snapVer, attempt, phase>>

Init ==

    /\ version = [r \in Calls |-> 0]
    /\ snapVer = [e \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ attempt = [e \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [e \in Cars |-> "idle"]

Read(e, r) ==
    /\ phase[e] = "idle"
    /\ r \notin served
    /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![e] = version[r]]
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![e] = r]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![e] = "trying"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<served, version>>

Commit(e) ==
    /\ phase[e] = "trying"
    /\ attempt[e] \notin served
    /\ version[attempt[e]] = snapVer[e]
    /\ served' = served \cup {attempt[e]}
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![attempt[e]] = version[attempt[e]] + 1]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![e] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snapVer, attempt>>

Retry(e) ==
    /\ phase[e] = "trying"
    /\ version[attempt[e]] # snapVer[e]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![e] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<served, version, snapVer, attempt>>

Withdraw(e) ==
    /\ phase[e] = "trying"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![e] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<served, version, snapVer, attempt>>

Interfere(r) ==
    /\ version[r] < MaxVer
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![r] = version[r] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<served, snapVer, attempt, phase>>

Done ==
    /\ served = Calls
    /\ \A e \in Cars : phase[e] = "idle"

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Cars, r \in Calls : Read(e, r)
    \/ \E e \in Cars : Commit(e)
    \/ \E e \in Cars : Retry(e)
    \/ \E e \in Cars : Withdraw(e)
    \/ \E r \in Calls : Interfere(r)
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    \A e \in Cars :
        (phase[e] = "trying" /\ attempt[e] \in served)
            => version[attempt[e]] > snapVer[e]

nl: Elevator cars in a bank compete to serve hall calls using optimistic locking with retry, where serving a call is an irreversible commitment that must happen at most once even though a car may run slow (working from a stale snapshot) without ever failing. A car runs Read on an as-yet-unserved call, taking a snapshot of that call's optimistic version counter and entering a trying phase. It then runs Commit, which fires only if the call is still unserved and its version counter still matches the snapshot: this serves the call irreversibly and bumps the version counter so any concurrent stale attempt is invalidated. A car whose snapshot no longer matches the current version runs Retry and returns to idle, while a car that simply gives up its bid runs Withdraw. Interfere models a competing or slow update advancing a call's version counter. When every call is served and all cars are idle the system idles through a terminal self-loop. SAFETY PROPERTY: Any car still trying to serve a call that has already been served must be holding a stale version snapshot strictly older than the call's current version, so it can never commit a second time.

nl: A wildfire surveillance swarm of drones elects a coordinating leader that hands out slots on a shared radio downlink of fixed bandwidth capacity, and it must tolerate a leader that has gone slow (but not failed) by failing over to a newer leader. A follower drone runs Nominate to become a candidate for the next term above the current leadership term. A candidate whose term is strictly higher than the recognized leadership term runs Elect to install itself as leader and raise the recognized term, while a candidate that cannot win runs StepDown to revert to a follower. A leader whose term has fallen behind a newer leadership term is marked slow by Suspect, and a suspected drone later runs Resume to rejoin as a live participant (it was slow, never failed). A leader that is not currently suspected runs Grant to give an idle follower a downlink slot of some weight, but only when the total bandwidth in use plus that weight stays within capacity; Release frees a drone's slot back to the pool. There is no separate terminal action because an elected leader always remains available to grant or release slots. SAFETY PROPERTY: The total downlink bandwidth in use across all drones never exceeds the fixed channel capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od3m2p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Inst == {1, 2}
Parts == {1, 2, 3}
Cap == 3

VARIABLES phase, req, yesVotes, replied, held, poolUsed

vars == <<phase, req, yesVotes, replied, held, poolUsed>>

HeldTotal == held[1] + held[2]

Init ==
    /\ phase = [i \in Inst |-> "idle"]
    /\ req = [i \in Inst |-> 0]
    /\ yesVotes = [i \in Inst |-> {}]
    /\ replied = [i \in Inst |-> {}]
    /\ held = [i \in Inst |-> 0]
    /\ poolUsed = 0

Request(i, k) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "idle"
    /\ req' = [req EXCEPT ![i] = k]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "voting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yesVotes, replied, held, poolUsed>>

ReplyYes(i, p) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ p \notin replied[i]
    /\ replied' = [replied EXCEPT ![i] = replied[i] \cup {p}]
    /\ yesVotes' = [yesVotes EXCEPT ![i] = yesVotes[i] \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, req, held, poolUsed>>

ReplyNo(i, p) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ p \notin replied[i]
    /\ replied' = [replied EXCEPT ![i] = replied[i] \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, req, yesVotes, held, poolUsed>>

Prepare(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ replied[i] = Parts
    /\ yesVotes[i] = Parts
    /\ poolUsed + HeldTotal + req[i] <= Cap
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = req[i]]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "prepared"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<req, yesVotes, replied, poolUsed>>

AbortNo(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ replied[i] = Parts
    /\ yesVotes[i] # Parts
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<req, yesVotes, replied, held, poolUsed>>

AbortFull(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ replied[i] = Parts
    /\ yesVotes[i] = Parts
    /\ poolUsed + HeldTotal + req[i] > Cap
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<req, yesVotes, replied, held, poolUsed>>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "prepared"
    /\ poolUsed' = poolUsed + held[i]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<req, yesVotes, replied>>

Done == \A i \in Inst : phase[i] \in {"committed", "aborted"}

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Inst, k \in 1..Cap : Request(i, k)
    \/ \E i \in Inst, p \in Parts : ReplyYes(i, p)
    \/ \E i \in Inst, p \in Parts : ReplyNo(i, p)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Prepare(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : AbortNo(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : AbortFull(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Commit(i)
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityRespected == poolUsed + HeldTotal <= Cap

====
nl: Two independent interbank settlement batches run a two-phase commit protocol over their participant banks while drawing reservations from one shared liquidity pool of fixed capacity. Each batch begins idle and issues a Request that fixes the amount of pool capacity it will need and moves it into a voting phase. Its participant banks respond one at a time: ReplyYes records an affirmative prepare vote and ReplyNo records a refusal, each marking that participant as having replied. Once every participant has replied, the coordinator resolves the batch: Prepare succeeds only when the vote was unanimously yes and the shared pool still has room for the requested amount on top of everything already held and committed, at which point the batch tentatively holds that capacity; AbortNo aborts a batch whose vote was not unanimous; and AbortFull aborts a unanimously-approved batch that cannot fit in the remaining pool. A prepared batch then runs Commit, converting its tentative hold into permanent committed pool usage. When both batches have committed or aborted the system idles via a terminal self-loop. SAFETY PROPERTY: The committed pool usage plus the capacity tentatively held by both settlement batches never exceeds the fixed pool capacity.
